<thought>Based on the mass spectrum (M⁺ at 127.10) and the NMR data (three singlet methyl groups totaling 12 H, with one methyl downfield at 2.65 ppm indicating attachment to a carbonyl, and two upfield methyls at 1.78 ppm (3 H) and 1.92 ppm (6 H) suggesting aromatic methyls), the most plausible structure is a phenyl ring fully substituted by three methyl groups (two equivalent, one distinct) and a carbonyl‑attached methyl (acetyl). This corresponds to the SMILES string “Cc1c(C)cc(C)c1C(=O)C”. The molecular formula derived from this SMILES is C₁₀H₁₂O, which matches the observed mass within experimental error. 

Thus, the SMILES string for the unknown sample is:

<final_answer>Cc1c(C)cc(C)c1C(=O)C</final_answer>
